components.name: Primary Button

components.name: Credibility Stat
components.description: Redesigned proof-stat unit for the landing page credibility bar — replaces the current plain-inline-text-plus-middot treatment. One of these per stat (178 score / Stanford Law / 200+ students coached / 3,000+ tutoring hours), laid out as equal-width columns with generous gap, not an inline run.
components.css: .ds-stat { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 2px; text-align: center; } .ds-stat-number { font-size: 1.5rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: -0.01em; color: oklch(46% 0.1 205); } .ds-stat-label { font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; color: oklch(54% 0.011 205); }

narrative.overview: DrillMap runs two registers under one roof. The public landing page is a brand surface where a skeptical, stressed LSAT student has to be convinced fast; the authenticated app is a product surface, a calm weekly tool a signed-up student returns to. Same tokens, same hue family, different energy. The Proof Trail is the philosophy for the brand register: real evidence (a 178 score, Stanford Law, 200+ students coached, 3,000+ tutoring hours, an actual sample weekly plan) is the whole conversion argument, and design should make that evidence physically impossible to skim past. The product register keeps the system's original restraint: a weekly-cadence tool should never look like it's competing for attention.
keyCharacteristics: One hue family (ink neutrals + accent blue-teal, both hued toward ~205) carries both registers
Brand-register moments commit to the accent at real scale; product-register moments keep it to ≤10% of the screen
Flat-by-default everywhere, with one sparing exception: brand-register hero/proof moments may take a soft shadow or solid-color block
Status and category are always conveyed through icon, label, or shape, never color alone

rules.name: The Register Determines the Rule
rules.body: Product-register surfaces obey the original Quiet Accent Rule: accent-600 on ≤10% of the screen, reserved for actionable elements. Brand-register surfaces are exempt from that ceiling by design.

rules.name: The Proof Number Rule
rules.body: Any number that is direct evidence of credibility or outcome is never rendered at body or label scale. It gets its own visual step: minimum Headline scale, accent-600 or ink-900, with its label demoted beneath it in Label scale.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. A shadow, if it appears, signals either a transient overlay or one of the named brand-register proof exceptions — never permanent app card structure.

dos: Do treat proof numbers as first-class visual elements on brand-register pages, per the Proof Number Rule.
Do keep the app strictly Restrained even as the landing page goes bolder. One brand, two registers.
Do use the single Geist Sans family with real weight/scale contrast to build hierarchy.
Do pair any status or state indicator with an icon or label, never color alone.
Do keep motion restrained everywhere: transitions only as direct feedback, 150ms ease-out, nothing choreographed.
donts: Don't build a generic SaaS template landing page.
Don't default to a corporate/legacy test-prep look.
Don't render credibility or outcome numbers at the same visual weight as surrounding body copy.
Don't carry the landing page's Committed color energy into the authenticated app, or vice versa.
Don't add shadows under static, resting app cards.
Don't introduce a second accent hue to make the landing page feel bolder.
